tests_notes: Present and absent targets, first occurrence among duplicates, negatives, empty inputs; workload: 20000 lookups in 100000 sorted items.

A.rationale: Each lookup is a binary search, O(log n). Indexing the first position of every value once makes each target a single dict probe, and setting a key only when it is new keeps the first occurrence.

B.strategy: List comprehension with an assignment expression
B.rationale: A comprehension replaces the explicit loop and the repeated append calls; the walrus keeps the bisect result for the bounds and equality checks.

C.strategy: Bind append and bisect to locals
C.rationale: Conservative micro-optimization: local names skip the attribute and global lookups inside the loop. The search and the result are unchanged.

notes: An honest no-win story: binary search with bisect is already right here. The dict pays for indexing all 100000 items to answer 20000 lookups; the comprehension and the local bindings are within noise.
